Name: agents.voice.enabled
Desc: Enable the Voice Mode panel in the chat view for voice-driven coding conversations.

Name: agents.voice.handsFree
Desc: When enabled, voice mode automatically re-enters listening after the assistant finishes speaking, so you can hold a hands-free back-and-forth conversation. When disabled, you start and end each turn manually, and ending the turn sends it. Turns are not ended automatically on trailing silence or a stop phrase unless `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` or `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` is explicitly configured.

Name: agents.voice.language
Desc: The language used for speech recognition, dictation, and spoken responses. The selectable languages support native voice output. Automatic uses the configured display language for speech recognition and dictation when supported; otherwise, it follows the system or browser locale. English voice output is used when the detected language does not support native voice output. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately.

Name: agents.voice.liveTranscript
Desc: Show your speech as a live, word-by-word transcript while you are speaking. When disabled, your transcript appears only once you finish speaking. Requires `agents.voice.showTranscript` to be enabled to be visible.

Name: agents.voice.showButton
Desc: Controls whether the Voice Mode button is shown in the chat input. When hidden, Voice Mode can still be started with its keyboard shortcut.

Name: agents.voice.showTranscript
Desc: Show the voice transcript overlay in the chat input area while voice mode is active. Enable this to read responses as text when `agents.voice.speakResponses` is disabled.

Name: agents.voice.speakResponses
Desc: When enabled, the assistant reads responses aloud. When disabled, responses are not spoken; enable `agents.voice.showTranscript` to read them as a text transcript instead.

Name: agents.voice.turn.silenceMs
Desc: Trailing silence in milliseconds before the backend ends the turn automatically. Set to `-1` to disable ending the turn on silence, in which case the turn ends only via a stop phrase (`agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`) or manually. When enabled, the backend clamps this to its supported range (currently 200-5000 ms) and is the source of truth. When hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is disabled, the turn is not ended on silence by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

Name: agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases
Desc: Phrases that end the turn when spoken at the end of an utterance. Leave empty to disable ending the turn on a stop phrase, in which case the turn ends only on trailing silence (`agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`) or manually. The backend strips the matched phrase from the transcript before it reaches the agent. When hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is disabled, stop phrases do not end the turn by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

Name: agents.voice.voice
Desc: The voice used when the assistant reads responses aloud. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately. Use [Voice Mode instructions](command:workbench.action.chat.configureVoiceInstructions) to customize Voice Mode behavior and terminology. - harper_neutral: Harper. - birch_neutral: Birch. - junho_neutral: Junho. - oak_neutral: Oak.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.advanced.runtime
Desc: Note: this setting is applicable only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. Key/value pairs are passed through to the root of the sandbox runtime configuration.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.allowAutoApprove
Desc: Controls whether agent mode terminal commands that run inside the sandbox are auto-approved. When disabled, the run in terminal tool uses the existing approval flow. This applies only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork
Desc: When `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled, controls whether to allow all network domains in the sandbox. When enabled, the sandbox preserves file system restrictions while relaxing all network restrictions.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands
Desc: Controls whether agent mode terminal commands can run outside the sandbox after user confirmation when a sandboxed command fails or when sandbox restrictions would block the command. This applies only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.enabled
Desc: Controls whether agent mode uses sandboxing to restrict what tools can do. When enabled, tools like the terminal are run in a sandboxed environment to limit access to the system. Use `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` to allow all network domains. - off: Disable sandboxing for agent mode tools. - on: Enable sandboxing for agent mode tools.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows
Desc: Controls whether agent mode uses sandboxing on Windows. Use `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` to allow all network domains. - off: Disable sandboxing for agent mode tools on Windows. - on: Enable sandboxing for agent mode tools on Windows.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.linux
Desc: Note: this setting is applicable only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. Controls file system access in sandbox on Linux. Paths do not support glob patterns, only literal paths (ex: ./src/, ~/.ssh, .env). **bubblewrap** and **socat** should be installed for this setting to work.

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.mac
Desc: Note: this setting is applicable only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. Controls file system access in sandbox on macOS. Paths also support git-style glob patterns(ex: *.ts, ./src, ./src/**/*.ts, file?.txt).

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.windows
Desc: Note: this setting is applicable only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. Controls file system access in sandbox on Windows. Paths do not support glob patterns, only literal paths (ex: C:\src, C:\Users\me\.ssh, .env).

Name: chat.agent.sandbox.retryWithAllowNetworkRequests
Desc: Controls whether agent mode terminal commands can retry in the sandbox with unrestricted network access after user confirmation. This applies only when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled and preserves file system sandboxing while relaxing network restrictions for an approved command.

Name: chat.agent.terminal.allowList
Desc: Use `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` instead

Name: chat.agent.terminal.autoApprove
Desc: Use `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` instead

Name: chat.agent.terminal.denyList
Desc: Use `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` instead

Name: chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove
Desc: A list of commands or regular expressions that control whether the run in terminal tool commands require explicit approval. These will be matched against the start of a command. A regular expression can be provided by wrapping the string in `/` characters followed by optional flags such as `i` for case-insensitivity. Set to `true` to automatically approve commands, `false` to always require explicit approval or `null` to unset the value. Note that these commands and regular expressions are evaluated for every _sub-command_ within the full _command line_, so `foo && bar` for example will need both `foo` and `bar` to match a `true` entry and must not match a `false` entry in order to auto approve. Inline commands such as `<(foo)` (process substitution) should also be detected. An object can be used to match against the full command line instead of matching sub-commands and inline commands, for example `{ approve: false, matchCommandLine: true }`. In order to be auto approved _both_ the sub-command and command line must not be explicitly denied, then _either_ all sub-commands or command line needs to be approved. Note that there's a default set of rules to allow and also deny commands. Consider setting `chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules` to `true` to ignore all default rules to ensure there are no conflicts with your own rules. Do this at your own risk, the default denial rules are designed to protect you against running dangerous commands. | `"mkdir": true` | Allow all commands starting with `mkdir` | `"npm run build": true` | Allow all commands starting with `npm run build` | `"bin/test.sh": true` | Allow all commands that match the path `bin/test.sh` (`bin\test.sh`, `./bin/test.sh`, etc.) | `"/^git (status\|show\\b.*)$/": true` | Allow `git status` and all commands starting with `git show` | `"/^Get-ChildItem\\b/i": true` | will allow `Get-ChildItem` commands regardless of casing | `"/.*/": true` | Allow all commands (denied commands still require approval) | `"rm": false` | Require explicit approval for all commands starting with `rm` | `"/\\.ps1/i": { approve: false, matchCommandLine: true }` | Require explicit approval for any _command line_ that contains `".ps1"` regardless of casing | `"rm": null` | Unset the default `false` value for `rm`

Name: chat.tools.terminal.autoApproveWorkspaceNpmScripts
Desc: Whether to automatically approve npm, yarn, and pnpm run commands when the script is defined in a workspace package.json file. Since the workspace is trusted, scripts defined in package.json are considered safe to run without explicit approval.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.backgroundNotifications
Desc: This setting is deprecated. Terminal completion and input-needed notifications are now always enabled. This setting is deprecated and no longer has any effect. Terminal completion and input-needed notifications are now always enabled for any command that continues running after the tool returns.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.blockDetectedFileWrites
Desc: Controls whether detected file write operations are blocked in the run in terminal tool. When detected, this will require explicit approval regardless of whether the command would normally be auto approved. Note that this cannot detect all possible methods of writing files, this is what is currently detected: - File redirection (detected via the bash or PowerShell tree sitter grammar) - `sed` in-place editing (`-i`, `-I`, `--in-place`) - never: Allow all detected file writes. - outsideWorkspace: Block file writes detected outside the workspace. This depends on the shell integration feature working correctly to determine the current working directory of the terminal. - all: Block all detected file writes.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove
Desc: Controls whether to allow auto approval in the run in terminal tool.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.enforceTimeoutFromModel
Desc: Whether to enforce the timeout value provided by the model in the run in terminal tool. When enabled, if the model provides a timeout parameter, the tool will stop tracking the command after that duration and return the output collected so far.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.idlePollInterval
Desc: Configures the idle poll interval in milliseconds used by the run in terminal tool to detect when commands have finished executing. Lower values make command detection faster but may cause false positives on slow systems. This primarily affects terminals without shell integration where idle detection is used instead of shell integration events.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.idleSilenceTimeoutMs
Desc: Number of milliseconds the run in terminal tool will wait for new output from a synchronous command before moving it to a background terminal and returning what was collected so far. The process is not killed — the tool returns the terminal ID so the model can poll, send input, or kill it. Set to `0` to disable.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules
Desc: Whether to ignore the built-in default auto-approve rules used by the run in terminal tool as defined in `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove`. When this setting is enabled, the run in terminal tool will ignore any rule that comes from the default set but still follow rules defined in the user, remote and workspace settings. Use this setting at your own risk; the default auto-approve rules are designed to protect you against running dangerous commands.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.outputCompaction
Desc: When enabled, the output of commands run by the run in terminal tool is compacted before being returned to the model, reducing the number of tokens spent on noisy output (for example progress bars or repeated log lines) while preserving the important information.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.outputDeltas
Desc: When enabled, repeated get terminal output tool calls return only output added since the previous poll for the same terminal execution, or a short unchanged-output message when there is no new output.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.outputLocation
Desc: Where to show the output from the run in terminal tool. - terminal: Reveal the terminal in the panel or editor in addition to chat. - chat: Reveal the terminal output within chat only.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.preventShellHistory
Desc: Whether to exclude commands run by the terminal tool from the shell history. See below for the supported shells and the method used for each: - `bash`: Sets `HISTCONTROL=ignorespace` and prepends the command with space - `zsh`: Sets `HIST_IGNORE_SPACE` option and prepends the command with space - `fish`: Sets `fish_private_mode` to prevent any command from entering history - `pwsh`: Sets a custom history handler via PSReadLine's `AddToHistoryHandler` to prevent any command from entering history

Name: chat.tools.terminal.shellIntegrationTimeout
Desc: Use `terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.timeout` instead Configures the duration in milliseconds to wait for shell integration to be detected when the run in terminal tool launches a new terminal. Set to `0` to skip the wait entirely, the default value `-1` uses a variable wait time based on the value of `terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled` and whether it's a remote window. A large value can be useful if your shell starts very slowly.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.terminalProfile.linux
Desc: The terminal profile to use on Linux for chat agent's run in terminal tool.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.terminalProfile.osx
Desc: The terminal profile to use on macOS for chat agent's run in terminal tool.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.terminalProfile.windows
Desc: The terminal profile to use on Windows for chat agent's run in terminal tool.

Name: chat.defaultToCopilotHarness
Desc: When enabled, new editor and panel chat sessions default to the Agent Host Copilot SDK instead of the local harness.

Name: chat.editor.localAgent.enabled
Desc: When enabled, shows the VS Code local chat harness in the chat picker. This setting is ignored in virtual workspaces, where the local chat harness is always available.

Name: chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness
Desc: When enabled, uses the Agent Host Copilot SDK whenever the local harness would otherwise be selected for a new editor chat session. Claude and Codex selections are unaffected.

Name: chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled
Desc: When enabled, extension-provided BYOK ('bring your own key') models can run in agent-host sessions. Changes are synchronized to the running agent host and do not require a restart.

Name: chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled
Desc: When enabled, the agent host registers the Claude provider, subject to the Claude SDK being reachable. The agent host process must be restarted for changes to take effect.

Name: chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled
Desc: When enabled, the agent host registers the Codex provider (subject to the Codex SDK being reachable). Enabling takes effect without restarting the agent host.

Name: chat.agentHost.experimental.activeAgentTitleGeneration
Desc: When enabled, the active agent names new sessions and chats using rename tools. When disabled, a utility model generates titles. Changes apply to sessions and chats created afterward.

Name: chat.agentHost.experimental.markdownPlanRichLinks
Desc: When enabled, agents receive guidance for using rich links to issues, pull requests, commits, sessions, and chats, plus running task markers, when creating or editing Markdown plan documents.

Name: chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled
Desc: When enabled, agent-host sessions include the GitHub MCP server.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.captureContent
Desc: When enabled, includes prompt and response content in OTel span attributes. Configurable in user settings only. Sets `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT`. Privacy-sensitive: do not enable in environments that ship spans to shared sinks.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.dbSpanExporter.enabled
Desc: When enabled, the agent host persists every emitted OTel span to a local SQLite database. Configurable in user settings only. Spans can be inspected via the `Export Agent Host Traces Database` command. Compatible with external exporters: spans are written to SQLite *and* forwarded to the user-configured sink.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.enabled
Desc: When enabled, the agent host emits OpenTelemetry traces from the Copilot SDK. Configurable in user settings only. Either configure `chat.agentHost.otel.otlpEndpoint` to ship traces to an external collector or enable `chat.agentHost.otel.dbSpanExporter.enabled` to capture them locally.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.exporterType
Desc: Exporter backend used by the Copilot SDK when `chat.agentHost.otel.enabled` is on. Configurable in user settings only. `otlp-grpc` is downgraded to `otlp-http` transparently in the CLI runtime.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.otlpEndpoint
Desc: OTLP endpoint URL when exporter type is `otlp-http` or `otlp-grpc`. Configurable in user settings only. Sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` inside the agent host process.

Name: chat.agentHost.otel.outfile
Desc: Output path for span JSON lines when exporter type is `file`. Configurable in user settings only. Sets `COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH`.

Name: chat.agentHost.systemProxy.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Copilot sessions automatically discover and use the operating system's proxy configuration when no proxy environment variable is set.

Name: chat.agentMerge.addressReviews
Desc: Controls whether enabled Agent Merge sessions address unresolved review threads, changes-requested reviews, and new pull request comments from repository maintainers or the Copilot pull request reviewer.

Name: chat.agentMerge.enabled
Desc: Enables the experimental Agent Merge controller and its commands. Agent Merge can monitor an agent session's pull request, ask the agent to address selected blockers, and optionally merge the pull request when it is ready.

Name: chat.agentMerge.fixCI
Desc: Controls whether enabled Agent Merge sessions ask the agent to fix failed required CI checks.

Name: chat.agentMerge.mergeMethod
Desc: Controls the native merge method used by Agent Merge. - auto: Uses the first repository-compatible method in this order: squash, merge commit, rebase. - squash: Uses squash merge when the repository permits it. - merge: Uses a merge commit when the repository permits it. - rebase: Uses rebase merge when the repository permits it.

Name: chat.agentMerge.mergePullRequest
Desc: Controls whether the Agent Host automatically merges or enqueues pull requests for enabled Agent Merge sessions after all selected maintenance work is complete.

Name: chat.agentMerge.replyAttribution
Desc: Controls whether review-thread replies posted by Agent Merge include an automated-reply attribution note.

Name: chat.agentMerge.resolveConflicts
Desc: Controls whether enabled Agent Merge sessions ask the agent to update branches that are behind or resolve merge conflicts.

Name: chat.artifactTools.enabled
Desc: When enabled, agents can record artifacts — pull requests, issues, commits, websites, files and other resources — which are surfaced above the chat input.

Name: chat.stickyScroll.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the current prompt is pinned to the top of the chat transcript while scrolling.

Name: chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains
Desc: Allowed domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser). Applies when `chat.agent.networkFilter` or `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. When `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` is enabled, all domains are allowed. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`. When both allowed and denied lists are empty, all domains are blocked. Denied domains (see `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains`) take precedence.

Name: chat.agent.codeBlockProgress
Desc: When applying edits, show a progress animation in the code block pill. If disabled, shows the progress percentage instead.

Name: chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses
Desc: Controls whether completed chat responses collapse intermediate work while keeping the final response visible.

Name: chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains
Desc: Denied domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser). Applies when `chat.agent.networkFilter` or `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled. This does not apply when `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` is enabled. Takes precedence over `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains`. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`.

Name: chat.agent.enabled
Desc: When enabled, agent mode can be activated from chat and tools in agentic contexts with side effects can be used.

Name: chat.agent.networkFilter
Desc: When enabled, network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) is restricted according to `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains` and `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains`. Domain filtering is also applied to those tools when `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` is enabled.

Name: chat.agent.thinking.collapsedTools
Desc: Controls how tool calls are displayed in relation to thinking sections. - off: Tool calls are shown separately, not collapsed into thinking. - withThinking: Tool calls are collapsed into thinking sections when thinking is present. - always: Tool calls are always collapsed, even without thinking.

Name: chat.agent.thinking.generateTitles
Desc: Controls whether to use an LLM to generate summary titles for thinking sections.

Name: chat.agent.thinking.phrases
Desc: Customize the loading messages shown during agent thinking and progress indicators. Use `"mode": "replace"` to use only your phrases, or `"mode": "append"` to add them to the defaults.

Name: chat.agent.thinking.terminalTools
Desc: When enabled, terminal tool calls are displayed inside the thinking dropdown with a simplified view.

Name: chat.agent.thinkingStyle
Desc: Controls how thinking is rendered. - collapsed: Thinking parts will be collapsed by default. - collapsedPreview: Thinking parts will be expanded first, then collapse once we reach a part that is not thinking. - fixedScrolling: Show thinking in a fixed-height streaming panel that auto-scrolls; click header to expand to full height.

Name: chat.agentFilesLocations
Desc: Specify location(s) of custom agent files (`*.agent.md`). [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-chat-modes). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.agentHost.agentDebugLog.enabled
Desc: Enable agent debug logging for agent host sessions: surface their debug events in the agent debug panel. Takes effect immediately; only sessions that run while this is enabled are captured.

Name: chat.agentHost.agentDebugLog.maxEventsInMemory
Desc: Maximum number of debug events kept in memory per agent host session for the agent debug panel. Older events beyond this limit are dropped from the in-memory buffer, which also lowers the totals (such as token usage) shown in the panel overview.

Name: chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled
Desc: When enabled, logs all AHP transport messages for agent host connections to JSONL files under the window's log directory.

Name: chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable
Desc: When enabled, Agent Host sessions remain available while signed out. The Agents window opens without forcing GitHub sign-in, and editor chat lets you select the Copilot harness. Agents usable without GitHub (for example Codex with ChatGPT authentication or Claude in native mode with your own Anthropic credentials) work while signed out; agents that require GitHub prompt you to add a model or sign in. When disabled (the default), GitHub sign-in is required before the Agents window opens.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings
Desc: When enabled, maps supported legacy VS Code settings to equivalent Copilot SDK managed settings for local Agent Host sessions. Only restrictions are mapped, and only from globally-scoped values — workspace and folder values are ignored. Applies to local sessions using the Copilot agent; remote hosts and other agents are unaffected. This compatibility bridge is temporary and is not used for new settings.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.modelCapabilityOverrides
Desc: Per-model capability overrides for Copilot SDK agent sessions, keyed by model id (`*` matches every model; a specific entry wins field-by-field), intended for evaluating models against an existing model's profile. Declare an aliased `family` (for example `claude-opus-4.8`) to route the model to that family's tuned system prompt and tool profile without changing the model id sent to the runtime — so a preview model can be evaluated against a known prompt while still running on its own endpoint — a `reasoningEffort` to pin its effort level, `availableTools`/`excludedTools` to filter its tool set, or `modelCapabilities` to override individual capability limits (e.g. vision support, context window size) passed through to the SDK. All overrides apply when a session launches or resumes. On a mid-session model change, only the new model's `reasoningEffort` is applied; the session keeps its launch-time family, tool filters, and model capabilities. Only affects Copilot agent sessions. **Note**: This is an advanced setting for experimentation.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.multiTurnContextRouting.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Auto model selection in Copilot SDK agent sessions routes on the conversation so far, sending prior user messages to the router instead of scoring the latest message alone.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.reasoningEffortOverride
Desc: Overrides the reasoning effort for Copilot SDK agent sessions regardless of the per-model picker value. Set it to a level the selected model supports (for example `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh`) — choosing a level the model does not support may be rejected by the model. A value that isn't a recognized effort level is ignored and the session falls back to the picker value. Applied when a session is created and when its model changes. Only affects Copilot CLI agent sessions. **Note**: This is an advanced setting for experimentation.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.reasoningSummary.enabled
Desc: When enabled, requests concise reasoning summaries for supported Copilot SDK agent sessions.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.toolSearch.deferThreshold
Desc: Minimum number of tools before MCP and external tools are deferred behind tool search. Set to 0 to always defer external tools. Only effective when tool search is enabled.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilot.toolSearch.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions defer MCP and non-core VS Code tools behind a tool-search tool so the model discovers them on demand instead of loading every tool definition up front.

Name: chat.agentHost.copilotSdk.logLevel
Desc: Controls the log level for the Copilot SDK runtime used by the local agent host. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client; active sessions are reloaded when next used. - info: Log informational messages. Running VS Code with trace logging still enables all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics. - trace: Log all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics.

Name: chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions use the Agent Host terminal tool override instead of the SDK's default terminal behavior.

Name: chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions running a Claude Opus 4.8 model apply Opus 4.8-tuned system-prompt section overrides on top of the default system message.

Name: chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabled
Desc: Sandbox mode for the Copilot SDK's built-in shell tool on macOS and Linux. Only takes effect when `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` is `false`; when the Agent Host's own terminal tool is enabled, the engine sandbox is controlled by `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`. The sandbox applies to every permission mode. Unrestricted network is controlled by `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork`. Use `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows` on Windows. - off: No sandbox policy is forwarded for the SDK's built-in shell tool — commands run unsandboxed. - on: The SDK's built-in shell tool runs inside a sandbox using the configured filesystem policy with outbound network blocked.

Name: chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows
Desc: Sandbox mode for the Copilot SDK's built-in shell tool on Windows. Only takes effect when `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` is `false`. This setting is independent of `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabled` so Windows sandbox support can be enabled separately. Unrestricted network is controlled by `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork`. - off: No sandbox policy is forwarded for the SDK's built-in shell tool on Windows — commands run unsandboxed. - on: The SDK's built-in shell tool runs inside the Windows sandbox using the configured filesystem policy.

Name: chat.agentsControl.enabled
Desc: Controls how the 'Agent Status' indicator appears in the title bar command center. When set to `hidden`, the indicator is not shown. Other values show the indicator and automatically enable `window.commandCenter`. The unread and in-progress session indicators require `chat.viewSessions.enabled` to be enabled. - hidden: The agent status indicator is hidden from the title bar. - badge: Shows the agent status as a badge next to the command center. - compact: Replaces the command center search box with a compact agent status indicator and unified chat widget.

Name: chat.agentSessionProjection.enabled
Desc: Controls whether Agent Session Projection mode is enabled for reviewing agent sessions in a focused workspace.

Name: chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli
Desc: Controls whether legacy extension host Copilot CLI chat sessions are migrated in place to the Agent host when opened, so their history becomes editable. When disabled, legacy sessions open as before.

Name: chat.agentSessions.showExternal
Desc: Controls which external agent sessions, created outside VS Code's Agent Host, are shown. - none: Only shows sessions created by the Agent Host. - recent: Shows up to the 2 most recently updated external sessions from the last 7 days, hiding any that you have started 2 newer sessions after. - last24Hours: Shows external sessions updated in the last 24 hours. - last7Days: Shows external sessions updated in the last 7 days. - last30Days: Shows external sessions updated in the last 30 days.

Name: chat.agentsHandoffTip.mode
Desc: Controls the tip shown above the chat input offering to continue eligible agent sessions in the Agents Window. - hidden: Never show the handoff tip. - default: Show the handoff tip with the default description. - custom: Show the handoff tip with an alternate description.

Name: chat.agentSkillsLocations
Desc: Specify location(s) of agent skills (`SKILL.md`) that can be used in Chat Sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-skills). Each path should contain skill subfolders with SKILL.md files (e.g., add `my-skills` if you have `my-skills/skillA/SKILL.md`). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.artifacts.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the artifacts view is available in chat.

Name: chat.artifacts.rules.byFilePath
Desc: Rules for extracting artifacts from written files by file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.

Name: chat.artifacts.rules.byMemoryFilePath
Desc: Rules for extracting artifacts from memory tool calls by memory file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.

Name: chat.artifacts.rules.byMimeType
Desc: Rules for extracting artifacts from tool results by MIME type. Maps MIME type patterns (e.g. 'image/*') to group configuration.

Name: chat.assistedPermissions.enabled
Desc: Controls whether Assisted permissions is shown in Agent Host approval pickers.

Name: chat.autopilot.advanced.enabled
Desc: Enables **Advanced Autopilot**, a single switch that turns on all advanced Autopilot behaviors that delegate more of the loop to the agent. Currently, after each Autopilot turn a small, fast model evaluates whether your original request is complete; if not, Autopilot keeps working using that evaluation as guidance for the next turn, instead of relying on the agent to signal completion itself.

Name: chat.autoReply
Desc: Automatically skip question carousels by telling the agent that the user is not available and to use its best judgment. This is an advanced setting and can lead to unintended choices or actions based on incomplete context.

Name: chat.byokUtilityModelDefault
Desc: Controls the default model used by built-in utility flows when the selected main agent model is a bring your own key (BYOK) model. This setting has no effect when the selected main agent model is provided by GitHub Copilot. A specific model configured in `chat.utilityModel` or `chat.utilitySmallModel` takes precedence. - none: Do not use a default utility model. - mainAgent: Use the selected BYOK main agent model. - copilot: Use the default GitHub Copilot utility models.

Name: chat.checkpoints.enabled
Desc: Enables checkpoints in chat. Checkpoints allow you to restore the chat to a previous state.

Name: chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges
Desc: Controls whether to show chat checkpoint file changes.

Name: chat.contextUsage.enabled
Desc: Show the context window usage indicator in the chat input.

Name: chat.copilot.semanticSearch.enabled
Desc: Controls whether Copilot Agent Host sessions can use VS Code's semantic workspace search. When disabled, semantic search is unavailable.

Name: chat.copilot.subagentModelGuidance.enabled
Desc: When enabled, Copilot SDK agent sessions instruct the model to keep subagents on their default model, setting the task tool's `model` parameter only when you explicitly name the model a subagent should run on. Applied when a session launches or resumes.

Name: chat.customizations.promptMigration.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor offers to convert prompt files into skills for agent-host harnesses, which ignore prompt files. When disabled, the migration card and sidebar shortcut are hidden.

Name: chat.customizations.structuredPreview.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor shows a structured preview for markdown customization files (agents, skills, instructions, prompts). When disabled, the editor always opens the raw markdown in the embedded code editor.

Name: chat.customizations.userDataMigration.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor offers to move agents and instructions stored in user data to the active agent-host harness, which ignores the user data location. When disabled, the migration card and sidebar shortcut are hidden.

Name: chat.defaultConfiguration
Desc: Controls the default configuration for new agent sessions (such as Copilot). You can still change the mode and approval behavior per session, and each session remembers what was used.

Name: chat.defaultModel
Desc: The default model for new chat conversations. Use "auto" to let Copilot pick a model, a model family name (such as "opus" or "gemini") to use the latest available model in that family, or a full model id. You can still switch the model within a conversation; each new conversation starts at this model.

Name: chat.detectParticipant.enabled
Desc: Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.

Name: chat.disableAIFeatures
Desc: Disable and hide built-in AI features provided by GitHub Copilot, including chat and inline suggestions.

Name: chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay
Desc: Delay after which changes made by chat are automatically accepted. Values are in seconds, `0` means disabled and `100` seconds is the maximum.

Name: chat.editing.confirmEditRequestRemoval
Desc: Whether to show a confirmation before removing a request and its associated edits.

Name: chat.editing.confirmEditRequestRetry
Desc: Whether to show a confirmation before retrying a request and its associated edits.

Name: chat.editing.explainChanges.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Explain button in the Chat panel and the Explain Changes context menu in the SCM view are shown. This is an experimental feature.

Name: chat.editing.openChangedFileInDiffEditor
Desc: Controls whether selecting a file in the changed files list of a chat response opens it in a diff editor showing the changes made by chat, or in a regular editor. Holding `kbstyle(Alt)` while selecting the file opens it with the opposite behavior.

Name: chat.editing.revealNextChangeOnResolve
Desc: Controls whether the editor automatically reveals the next change after keeping or undoing a chat edit.

Name: chat.editor.codex.preferAgentHost
Desc: When enabled, Codex sessions opened from the regular workbench (sidebar chat) run inside the agent host process using the Codex App Server instead of the OpenAI extension. Only one Codex implementation surfaces per window. Requires `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled`.

Name: chat.editor.fontFamily
Desc: Controls the font family in chat codeblocks.

Name: chat.editor.fontSize
Desc: Controls the font size in pixels in chat codeblocks.

Name: chat.editor.fontWeight
Desc: Controls the font weight in chat codeblocks.

Name: chat.editor.lineHeight
Desc: Controls the line height in pixels in chat codeblocks. Use 0 to compute the line height from the font size.

Name: chat.editor.wordWrap
Desc: Controls whether lines should wrap in chat codeblocks.

Name: chat.editorAssociations
Desc: Configure [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) to editors for opening files from chat (for example `"*.md": "vscode.markdown.preview.editor"`).

Name: chat.editRequests
Desc: Enables editing of requests in the chat. This allows you to change the request content and resubmit it to the model.

Name: chat.exitAfterDelegation
Desc: Controls whether the chat panel automatically exits after delegating a request to another session.

Name: chat.experimental.collectInstructionsInExtension
Desc: When enabled, automatic instruction collection (.instructions.md, agent instructions, customizations index) is performed by the GitHub Copilot Chat extension instead of the core workbench.

Name: chat.experimental.detectParticipant.enabled
Desc: This setting is deprecated. Please use `chat.detectParticipant.enabled` instead. Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.

Name: chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.animationStyle
Desc: Controls the animation style for incremental rendering. - none: No animation. Content appears instantly. - fade: Simple opacity fade from 0 to 1. - rise: Content fades in while rising upward. - blur: Content fades in from a blurred state. - scale: Content scales up from slightly smaller. - slide: Content slides in from the left. - reveal: Content reveals top-to-bottom with a soft gradient edge.

Name: chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.buffering
Desc: Controls how content is buffered before rendering during incremental rendering. Lower buffering levels render faster but may show incomplete sentences or partially formed markdown. - off: Renders content immediately as tokens arrive. - word: Reveals content word by word. - paragraph: Buffers content until a paragraph break before rendering.

Name: chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.enabled
Desc: Enables incremental rendering with optional block-level animation when streaming chat responses.

Name: chat.experimental.permissionsSandboxToggle.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the permissions picker shows a "Sandboxing for terminal" toggle. Local sessions show it on the Default permissions option; Copilot Agent Host sessions show it as a separate setting that applies to every permission mode. For Copilot SDK sessions using the built-in shell tool, the toggle reflects and updates `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabled` or `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows`.

Name: chat.experimental.richLinks.enabled
Desc: Controls whether supported links in chat are rendered as rich links with live metadata. Enabling this may make authenticated requests to services such as GitHub.

Name: chat.experimental.sessionArchiveActionWording
Desc: Controls the wording and icons used by actions that archive and unarchive chat sessions, as well as the label of the archived sessions section. - archive: Use Archive, Archive All, Unarchive, and Unarchive All. - done: Use Mark as Done, Mark All as Done, Restore, and Restore All.

Name: chat.experimental.stickyScroll.enabled
Desc: Controls whether chat requests use experimental tree-based sticky scroll instead of the sticky prompt header.

Name: chat.experimental.useSkillAdherencePrompt
Desc: Controls whether a stronger skill adherence prompt is used that encourages the model to immediately invoke skills when relevant rather than just announcing them. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.experimentalSessionsWindowOverride
Desc: When true, enables sessions-window-specific behavior for extensions.

Name: chat.exploreAgent.defaultModel
Desc: Select the default language model to use for the Explore subagent from the available providers. - : Use the vendor's default model

Name: chat.extensionTools.enabled
Desc: Enable using tools contributed by third-party extensions.

Name: chat.extensionUnification.enabled
Desc: Enables the unification of GitHub Copilot extensions. When enabled, all GitHub Copilot functionality is served from the GitHub Copilot Chat extension. When disabled, the GitHub Copilot and GitHub Copilot Chat extensions operate independently.

Name: chat.fontFamily
Desc: Controls the font family in chat messages.

Name: chat.fontSize
Desc: Controls the font size in pixels in chat messages.

Name: chat.growthNotification.enabled
Desc: Controls whether to show a growth notification in the agent sessions view to encourage new users to try Copilot.

Name: chat.hookFilesLocations
Desc: Specify paths to hook configuration files that define custom shell commands to execute at strategic points in an agent's workflow. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-chat-hooks). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. Supports Copilot hooks (`*.json`) and Claude Code hooks (`settings.json`, `settings.local.json`). This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.implicitContext.enabled
Desc: Enables automatically using the active editor as chat context for specified chat locations.

Name: chat.implicitContext.includeActiveEditor
Desc: When enabled, the active editor is automatically forwarded as context, even when it would otherwise only be suggested. Selections and explicitly attached files are always included regardless of this setting. Note: this setting currently only applies to Agent Host sessions (such as Copilot).

Name: chat.implicitContext.suggestedContext
Desc: Controls whether the new implicit context flow is shown. In Ask and Edit modes, the context will automatically be included. When using an agent, context will be suggested as an attachment. Selections are always included as context.

Name: chat.includeApplyingInstructions
Desc: Controls whether instructions with a matching 'applyTo' attribute are automatically included in chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.includeReferencedInstructions
Desc: Controls whether referenced instructions are automatically included in chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.inlineChat.agentHost.enabled
Desc: Controls whether editor inline chat is backed by the Agent Host instead of the extension host. Applied on startup.

Name: chat.inlineReferences.style
Desc: Controls how file and symbol references are displayed in chat messages. - box: Display file and symbol references as boxed widgets with icons. - link: Display file and symbol references as simple blue links without icons.

Name: chat.instructionsFilesLocations
Desc: Specify location(s) of instructions files (`*.instructions.md`) that can be attached in Chat sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-instructions). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.math.enabled
Desc: Enable math rendering in chat responses using KaTeX.

Name: chat.mcp.access
Desc: Controls access to installed Model Context Protocol servers. - none: No access to MCP servers. - registry: Allows access to MCP servers listed in the registry that VS Code is connected to. - all: Allow access to any installed MCP server.

Name: chat.mcp.apps.enabled
Desc: Controls whether MCP servers can provide custom UI for tool invocations.

Name: chat.mcp.assisted.nuget.enabled
Desc: Enables NuGet packages for AI-assisted MCP server installation. Used to install MCP servers by name from the central registry for .NET packages (NuGet.org).

Name: chat.mcp.autostart
Desc: Controls whether MCP servers should be automatically started when the chat messages are submitted. - never: Never automatically start MCP servers. - onlyNew: Only automatically start new MCP servers that have never been run. - newAndOutdated: Automatically start new and outdated MCP servers that are not yet running.

Name: chat.mcp.collisionBehavior
Desc: Controls behavior when multiple MCP servers are discovered with the same name. 'disable' disables lower-priority duplicates. 'suffix' appends numeric suffixes to disambiguate. - disable: Disable lower-priority servers with duplicate names. - suffix: Append numeric suffixes to servers with duplicate names.

Name: chat.mcp.discovery.enabled
Desc: Configures discovery of Model Context Protocol servers from configuration from various other applications.

Name: chat.mcp.gallery.enabled
Desc: Enables the default Marketplace for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

Name: chat.mcp.serverSampling
Desc: Configures which models are exposed to MCP servers for sampling (making model requests in the background). This setting can be edited in a graphical way under the `MCP: List Servers` command.

Name: chat.modeFilesLocations
Desc: This setting is deprecated and will be removed in future releases. Chat modes are now called custom agents and are located in `.github/agents` Specify location(s) of custom chat mode files (`*.chatmode.md`). [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-chat-modes). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.newSession.defaultMode
Desc: The default mode for new chat sessions. When empty, the chat view's default mode is used.

Name: chat.notifyWindowOnConfirmation
Desc: Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a confirmation or question needs input. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast. - off: Never show OS notifications for confirmations. - windowNotFocused: Show OS notifications for confirmations when the window is not focused. - always: Always show OS notifications for confirmations, even when the window is focused.

Name: chat.notifyWindowOnResponseReceived
Desc: Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a response is received. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast. - off: Never show OS notifications for responses. - windowNotFocused: Show OS notifications for responses when the window is not focused. - always: Always show OS notifications for responses, even when the window is focused.

Name: chat.pasteAsAttachmentThreshold
Desc: The number of characters a paste must exceed before it is added to the chat input as an attachment instead of being inserted inline. A paste must also span several lines, so a long single-line paste is always inserted inline. Set this to a very large number to always paste inline.

Name: chat.permissions.default
Desc: Controls the default permissions picker mode for new local chat sessions. You can still change the permission mode per session, and each session remembers the permission mode that was used. If enterprise policy disables auto approval, new sessions use Default Permissions. - default: Start new chat sessions with Default Permissions. - autoApprove: Start new chat sessions in Bypass Approvals mode. - autopilot: Start new chat sessions in Autopilot mode.

Name: chat.planAgent.defaultModel
Desc: Select the default language model to use for the Plan agent from the available providers. - : Use the vendor's default model

Name: chat.pluginLocations
Desc: Plugin directories to discover. Each key is a path that points directly to a plugin folder, and the value enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) it. Paths can be absolute, relative to the workspace root, or start with `~/` for the user's home directory.

Name: chat.plugins.enabled
Desc: Enable agent plugin integration in chat.

Name: chat.plugins.enabledPlugins
Desc: Controls which [agent plugins](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-plugins) are enabled or disabled. Keys are plugin IDs in `<plugin>@<marketplace>` form (where marketplace is defined in `chat.plugins.marketplaces`); values enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) the plugin. Discovered alongside the path-keyed entries in `chat.pluginLocations`. When set by policy, entries are additive: plugins mapped to `true` are enabled in addition to the user's own plugins, and only plugins mapped to `false` are blocked from loading.

Name: chat.plugins.marketplaces
Desc: Plugin marketplaces to query. Entries may be GitHub shorthand (`owner/repo` or `owner/repo#ref`), direct Git repository URIs (`https://...git`, `ssh://...git`, or `git@host:path.git`, each optionally suffixed with `#ref`), or local repository URIs (`file:///...`). Equivalent GitHub shorthand and URI entries are deduplicated.

Name: chat.plugins.strictMarketplaces
Desc: Enterprise-managed allowlist of plugin marketplace sources. When set, only marketplaces matching one of these entries can be installed; an empty array blocks all marketplaces. This does not retroactively disable already-installed plugins. Each entry is an object with a `source` discriminator (`github`, `git`, `url`, `npm`, `file`, `directory`, `hostPattern`, or `pathPattern`) and the corresponding fields. Typically delivered via enterprise policy.

Name: chat.progressBorder.enabled
Desc: Show an animated gradient border around the chat input while the agent is working or thinking. Has no effect when reduced motion is enabled.

Name: chat.promptFilesLocations
Desc: Specify location(s) of reusable prompt files (`*.prompt.md`) that can be run in Chat sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-prompt-snippets). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.promptFilesRecommendations
Desc: Configure which prompt files to recommend in the chat welcome view. Each key is a prompt file name, and the value can be `true` to always recommend, `false` to never recommend, or a [when clause](https://aka.ms/vscode-when-clause) expression like `resourceExtname == .js` or `resourceLangId == markdown`.

Name: chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction
Desc: Controls which action is the default for the queue button when a request is in progress. - queue: Queue the message to send after the current request completes. - steer: Steer the current request by sending the message immediately, signaling the current request to yield.

Name: chat.restoreLastPanelSession
Desc: Controls whether the last session is restored in panel after restart.

Name: chat.saveBeforeSend
Desc: Controls whether all dirty editors except untitled editors are saved before sending a chat message.

Name: chat.sessionSync.enabled
Desc: Enable session sync to GitHub.com. When enabled, Copilot session data is synced to your GitHub account for cross-device access and richer insights. Requires `github.copilot.chat.localIndex.enabled` to also be enabled.

Name: chat.sessionSync.excludeRepositories
Desc: Repository patterns to exclude from session sync. Use exact `owner/repo` names or glob patterns like `my-org/*`. Sessions from matching repositories will only be stored locally.

Name: chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents
Desc: Controls whether subagents can invoke other subagents. When enabled, nesting is limited to a maximum depth of 5.

Name: chat.subagents.useRichRendering
Desc: Controls whether subagents in chat editors use a rich presentation that opens each subagent in its own editor instead of rendering its full activity inline in the parent chat.

Name: chat.terminal.agentHost.enabled
Desc: Controls whether Terminal Chat is backed by the Agent Host instead of the extension host. Applied on startup.

Name: chat.tips.enabled
Desc: Controls whether tips are shown above user messages in chat. New tips are added frequently, so this is a helpful way to stay up to date with the latest features.

Name: chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Open in Agents Window button is shown in the title bar.

Name: chat.titleBar.signIn.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the Copilot Sign In button is shown in the title bar when signed out. When disabled, the Sign In affordance falls back to the status bar.

Name: chat.tools.autoExpandFailures
Desc: When enabled, terminal tool failures are automatically expanded in the chat UI to show error details.

Name: chat.tools.compressOutput.enabled
Desc: Post-process tool output (for example `git diff`, `ls -l`, or `npm install`) to reduce token usage before it is sent to the model.

Name: chat.tools.confirmationCarousel.enabled
Desc: When enabled, multiple tool confirmations are batched into a carousel above the input.

Name: chat.tools.edits.autoApprove
Desc: Controls whether edits made by the agent are automatically approved. The default is to approve all edits except those made to certain files which have the potential to cause immediate unintended side-effects, such as `**/.vscode/*.json`. Set to `true` to automatically approve edits to matching files, `false` to always require explicit approval. The last pattern matching a given file will determine whether the edit is automatically approved.

Name: chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval
Desc: Controls which tools are eligible for automatic approval. Tools set to 'false' will always present a confirmation and will never offer the option to auto-approve. The default behavior (or setting a tool to 'true') may result in the tool offering auto-approval options.

Name: chat.tools.global.autoApprove
Desc: Global auto approve also known as "YOLO mode" disables manual approval completely for _all tools in all workspaces_, allowing the agent to act fully autonomously. This is extremely dangerous and is *never* recommended, even containerized environments like [Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces) and [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) have user keys forwarded into the container that could be compromised. **This feature disables [critical security protections](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/security) and makes it much easier for an attacker to compromise the machine.** Note: This setting only controls tool approval and does not prevent the agent from asking questions. To automatically answer agent questions, use the [`chat.autoReply`](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22chat.autoReply%22%5D) setting.

Name: chat.tools.riskAssessment.enabled
Desc: When enabled, tool confirmations show an LLM-generated risk level (Safe / Caution / Review carefully) and a short explanation.

Name: chat.tools.riskAssessment.model
Desc: The language model id used to generate tool risk assessments. Should be a small, fast model.

Name: chat.tools.terminal.simpleCollapsible
Desc: When enabled, terminal tool calls are always displayed in a collapsible container with a simplified view.

Name: chat.tools.todos.showWidget
Desc: Controls whether to show the todo list widget above the chat input. When enabled, the widget displays todo items created by the agent and updates as progress is made.

Name: chat.tools.urls.autoApprove
Desc: Controls which URLs are automatically approved when requested by chat tools. Keys are URL patterns and values can be `true` to approve both requests and responses, `false` to deny, or an object with `approveRequest` and `approveResponse` properties for granular control. - `"https://example.com": true` - Approve all requests to example.com - `"https://*.example.com": true` - Approve all requests to any subdomain of example.com - `"https://example.com/api/*": { "approveRequest": true, "approveResponse": false }` - Approve requests but not responses for example.com/api paths

Name: chat.turnStatusPills
Desc: Controls whether agent status pills are shown above the chat input while a turn is in progress and inside the completed response. Only applies to agent sessions.

Name: chat.undoRequests.restoreInput
Desc: Controls whether the input of the chat should be restored when an undo request is made. The input will be filled with the text of the request that was restored.

Name: chat.unifiedAgentsBar.enabled
Desc: Replaces the command center search box with a unified chat and search widget.

Name: chat.upvoteAnimation
Desc: Controls whether an animation is shown when clicking the thumbs up button on a chat response. - off: No animation is shown. - confetti: Shows a confetti burst animation around the thumbs up button. - floatingThumbs: Shows floating thumbs up icons rising from the button. - pulseWave: Shows expanding pulse rings from the button. - radiantLines: Shows radiant lines emanating from the button.

Name: chat.useAgentSkills
Desc: Controls whether skills are provided as specialized capabilities to the chat requests. Skills are loaded from the folders configured in `chat.agentSkillsLocations`. The language model can load these skills on-demand if the `read` tool is available. Learn more about [Agent Skills](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-skills). This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useAgentsMdFile
Desc: Controls whether instructions from `AGENTS.md` file found in a workspace roots are attached to all chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useClaudeHooks
Desc: Controls whether hooks from Claude configuration files can execute. When disabled, only Copilot-format hooks are used. Hooks are loaded from the files configured in `chat.hookFilesLocations`. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useClaudeMdFile
Desc: Controls whether instructions from `CLAUDE.md` file found in workspace roots, .claude and ~/.claude folder are attached to all chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useCustomizationsInParentRepositories
Desc: Controls whether to use chat customization files in parent repositories. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useHooks
Desc: Controls whether chat hooks are executed at strategic points during an agent's workflow. Hooks are loaded from the files configured in `chat.hookFilesLocations`. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles
Desc: Controls whether instructions from nested `AGENTS.md` files found in the workspace are listed in all chat requests. The language model can load these skills on-demand if the `read` tool is available. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

Name: chat.utilityModel
Desc: Override the language model used by built-in utility flows. Leave empty to use the configured default behavior. - : Use the default behavior for utility models

Name: chat.utilitySmallModel
Desc: Override the language model used by built-in small/fast utility flows. A fast and inexpensive model is recommended. Leave empty to use the configured default behavior. - : Use the default behavior for utility models

Name: chat.verbose
Desc: Show request and completion timestamps. Hover over a completion timestamp to show the elapsed response time.

Name: chat.viewProgressBadge.enabled
Desc: Show a progress badge on the chat view when an agent session is in progress that is opened in that view.

Name: chat.viewSessions.enabled
Desc: Show chat agent sessions when chat is empty or to the side when chat view is wide enough.

Name: chat.viewSessions.orientation
Desc: Controls the orientation of the chat agent sessions view when it is shown alongside the chat. - stacked: Display chat sessions vertically stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible. - sideBySide: Display chat sessions side by side if space is sufficient, otherwise fallback to stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible.

Name: comments.collapseOnResolve
Desc: Controls whether the comment thread should collapse when the thread is resolved.

Name: comments.maxHeight
Desc: Controls whether the comments widget scrolls or expands.

Name: comments.openPanel
Desc: This setting is deprecated in favor of `comments.openView`. Controls when the comments panel should open.

Name: comments.openView
Desc: Controls when the comments view should open. - never: The comments view will never be opened. - file: The comments view will open when a file with comments is active. - firstFile: If the comments view has not been opened yet during this session it will open the first time during a session that a file with comments is active. - firstFileUnresolved: If the comments view has not been opened yet during this session and the comment is not resolved, it will open the first time during a session that a file with comments is active.

Name: comments.thread.confirmOnCollapse
Desc: Controls whether a confirmation dialog is shown when collapsing a comment thread. - whenHasUnsubmittedComments: Show a confirmation dialog when collapsing a comment thread with unsubmitted comments. - never: Never show a confirmation dialog when collapsing a comment thread.

Name: comments.useRelativeTime
Desc: Determines if relative time will be used in comment timestamps (ex. '1 day ago').

Name: comments.visible
Desc: Controls the visibility of the comments bar and comment threads in editors that have commenting ranges and comments. Comments are still accessible via the Comments view and will cause commenting to be toggled on in the same way running the command "Comments: Toggle Editor Commenting" toggles comments.

Name: css.completion.completePropertyWithSemicolon
Desc: Insert semicolon at end of line when completing CSS properties.

Name: css.completion.triggerPropertyValueCompletion
Desc: By default, VS Code triggers property value completion after selecting a CSS property. Use this setting to disable this behavior.

Name: css.customData
Desc: A list of relative file paths pointing to JSON files following the [custom data format](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-css-languageservice/blob/master/docs/customData.md). VS Code loads custom data on startup to enhance its CSS support for CSS custom properties (variables), at-rules, pseudo-classes, and pseudo-elements you specify in the JSON files. The file paths are relative to workspace and only workspace folder settings are considered.

Name: css.format.braceStyle
Desc: Put braces on the same line as rules (`collapse`) or put braces on own line (`expand`).

Name: css.format.enable
Desc: Enable/disable default CSS formatter.

Name: css.format.maxPreserveNewLines
Desc: Maximum number of line breaks to be preserved in one chunk, when `css.format.preserveNewLines` is enabled.

Name: css.format.newlineBetweenRules
Desc: Separate rulesets by a blank line.

Name: css.format.newlineBetweenSelectors
Desc: Separate selectors with a new line.

Name: css.format.preserveNewLines
Desc: Whether existing line breaks before rules and declarations should be preserved.

Name: css.format.spaceAroundSelectorSeparator
Desc: Ensure a space character around selector separators `>`, `+`, `~` (e.g. `a > b`).

Name: css.hover.documentation
Desc: Show property and value documentation in CSS hovers.

Name: css.hover.references
Desc: Show references to MDN in CSS hovers.

Name: css.lint.argumentsInColorFunction
Desc: Invalid number of parameters.

Name: css.lint.boxModel
Desc: Do not use `width` or `height` when using `padding` or `border`.

Name: css.lint.compatibleVendorPrefixes
Desc: When using a vendor-specific prefix make sure to also include all other vendor-specific properties.

Name: css.lint.duplicateProperties
Desc: Do not use duplicate style definitions.

Name: css.lint.emptyRules
Desc: Do not use empty rulesets.

Name: css.lint.float
Desc: Avoid using `float`. Floats lead to fragile CSS that is easy to break if one aspect of the layout changes.

Name: css.lint.fontFaceProperties
Desc: `@font-face` rule must define `src` and `font-family` properties.

Name: css.lint.hexColorLength
Desc: Hex colors must consist of 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex numbers.

Name: css.lint.idSelector
Desc: Selectors should not contain IDs because these rules are too tightly coupled with the HTML.

Name: css.lint.ieHack
Desc: IE hacks are only necessary when supporting IE7 and older.

Name: css.lint.important
Desc: Avoid using `!important`. It is an indication that the specificity of the entire CSS has gotten out of control and needs to be refactored.

Name: css.lint.importStatement
Desc: Import statements do not load in parallel.

Name: css.lint.propertyIgnoredDueToDisplay
Desc: Property is ignored due to the display. E.g. with `display: inline`, the `width`, `height`, `margin-top`, `margin-bottom`, and `float` properties have no effect.

Name: css.lint.universalSelector
Desc: The universal selector (`*`) is known to be slow.

Name: css.lint.unknownAtRules
Desc: Unknown at-rule.

Name: css.lint.unknownProperties
Desc: Unknown property.

Name: css.lint.unknownVendorSpecificProperties
Desc: Unknown vendor specific property.

Name: css.lint.validProperties
Desc: A list of properties that are not validated against the `unknownProperties` rule.

Name: css.lint.vendorPrefix
Desc: When using a vendor-specific prefix, also include the standard property.

Name: css.lint.zeroUnits
Desc: No unit for zero needed.

Name: css.trace.server
Desc: Traces the communication between VS Code and the CSS language server.

Name: css.validate
Desc: Enables or disables all validations.

Name: debug.allowBreakpointsEverywhere
Desc: Allow setting breakpoints in any file.

Name: debug.autoExpandLazyVariables
Desc: Controls whether variables that are lazily resolved, such as getters, are automatically resolved and expanded by the debugger. - auto: When in screen reader optimized mode, automatically expand lazy variables. - on: Always automatically expand lazy variables. - off: Never automatically expand lazy variables.

Name: debug.breakpointsView.presentation
Desc: Controls whether breakpoints are displayed in a tree view grouped by file, or as a flat list.

Name: debug.closeReadonlyTabsOnEnd
Desc: At the end of a debug session, all the read-only tabs associated with that session will be closed

Name: debug.confirmOnExit
Desc: Controls whether to confirm when the window closes if there are active debug sessions. - never: Never confirm. - always: Always confirm if there are debug sessions.

Name: debug.console.acceptSuggestionOnEnter
Desc: Controls whether suggestions should be accepted on Enter in the Debug Console. Enter is also used to evaluate whatever is typed in the Debug Console.

Name: debug.console.closeOnEnd
Desc: Controls if the Debug Console should be automatically closed when the debug session ends.

Name: debug.console.collapseIdenticalLines
Desc: Controls if the Debug Console should collapse identical lines and show a number of occurrences with a badge.

Name: debug.console.fontFamily
Desc: Controls the font family in the Debug Console.

Name: debug.console.fontSize
Desc: Controls the font size in pixels in the Debug Console.

Name: debug.console.historySuggestions
Desc: Controls if the Debug Console should suggest previously typed input.

Name: debug.console.lineHeight
Desc: Controls the line height in pixels in the Debug Console. Use 0 to compute the line height from the font size.

Name: debug.console.maximumLines
Desc: Controls the maximum number of lines in the Debug Console.

Name: debug.console.wordWrap
Desc: Controls if the lines should wrap in the Debug Console.

Name: debug.disassemblyView.showSourceCode
Desc: Show Source Code in Disassembly View.

Name: debug.enableStatusBarColor
Desc: Color of the status bar when the debugger is active.

Name: debug.focusEditorOnBreak
Desc: Controls whether the editor should be focused when the debugger breaks.

Name: debug.focusWindowOnBreak
Desc: Controls whether the workbench window should be focused when the debugger breaks.

Name: debug.gutterMiddleClickAction
Desc: Controls the action to perform when clicking the editor gutter with the middle mouse button. - logpoint: Add Logpoint. - conditionalBreakpoint: Add Conditional Breakpoint. - triggeredBreakpoint: Add Triggered Breakpoint. - none: Don't perform any action.

Name: debug.hideLauncherWhileDebugging
Desc: Hide 'Start Debugging' control in title bar of 'Run and Debug' view while debugging is active. Only relevant when `debug.toolBarLocation` is not `docked`.

Name: debug.hideSlowPreLaunchWarning
Desc: Hide the warning shown when a `preLaunchTask` has been running for a while.

Name: debug.inlineValues
Desc: Show variable values inline in editor while debugging. - on: Always show variable values inline in editor while debugging. - off: Never show variable values inline in editor while debugging. - auto: Show variable values inline in editor while debugging when the language supports inline value locations.

Name: debug.internalConsoleOptions
Desc: Controls when the internal Debug Console should open.

Name: debug.onTaskErrors
Desc: Controls what to do when errors are encountered after running a preLaunchTask. - debugAnyway: Ignore task errors and start debugging. - showErrors: Show the Problems view and do not start debugging. - prompt: Prompt user. - abort: Cancel debugging.

Name: debug.openDebug
Desc: Controls when the debug view should open.

Name: debug.openExplorerOnEnd
Desc: Automatically open the explorer view at the end of a debug session.

Name: debug.saveBeforeStart
Desc: Controls what editors to save before starting a debug session. - allEditorsInActiveGroup: Save all editors in the active group before starting a debug session. - nonUntitledEditorsInActiveGroup: Save all editors in the active group except untitled ones before starting a debug session. - none: Don't save any editors before starting a debug session.

Name: debug.showBreakpointsInOverviewRuler
Desc: Controls whether breakpoints should be shown in the overview ruler.

Name: debug.showInlineBreakpointCandidates
Desc: Controls whether inline breakpoints candidate decorations should be shown in the editor while debugging.

Name: debug.showInStatusBar
Desc: Controls when the debug status bar item should be visible. - never: Never show debug item in status bar - always: Always show debug item in status bar - onFirstSessionStart: Show debug item in status bar only after debug was started for the first time

Name: debug.showSubSessionsInToolBar
Desc: Controls whether the debug sub-sessions are shown in the debug tool bar. When this setting is false the stop command on a sub-session will also stop the parent session.

Name: debug.showVariableTypes
Desc: Show variable type in variable pane during debug session

Name: debug.terminal.clearBeforeReusing
Desc: Before starting a new debug session in an integrated or external terminal, clear the terminal.

Name: debug.toolBarLocation
Desc: Controls the location of the debug toolbar. Either `floating` in all views, `docked` in the debug view, `commandCenter` (requires `window.commandCenter`), or `hidden`. - floating: Show debug toolbar in all views. - docked: Show debug toolbar only in debug views. - commandCenter: `(Experimental)` Show debug toolbar in the command center. - hidden: Do not show debug toolbar.

Name: debug.javascript.autoAttachFilter
Desc: Configures which processes to automatically attach and debug when `debug.node.autoAttach` is on. A Node process launched with the `--inspect` flag will always be attached to, regardless of this setting. - always: Auto attach to every Node.js process launched in the terminal. - smart: Auto attach when running scripts that aren't in a node_modules folder. - onlyWithFlag: Only auto attach when the `--inspect` is given. - disabled: Auto attach is disabled and not shown in status bar.

Name: debug.javascript.autoAttachSmartPattern
Desc: Configures glob patterns for determining when to attach in "smart" `debug.javascript.autoAttachFilter` mode. `$KNOWN_TOOLS$` is replaced with a list of names of common test and code runners. [Read more on the VS Code docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/nodejs/nodejs-debugging#_auto-attach-smart-patterns).

Name: debug.javascript.automaticallyTunnelRemoteServer
Desc: When debugging a remote web app, configures whether to automatically tunnel the remote server to your local machine.

Name: debug.javascript.breakOnConditionalError
Desc: Whether to stop when conditional breakpoints throw an error.

Name: debug.javascript.codelens.npmScripts
Desc: Where a "Run" and "Debug" code lens should be shown in your npm scripts. It may be on "all", scripts, on "top" of the script section, or "never".

Name: debug.javascript.debugByLinkOptions
Desc: Options used when debugging open links clicked from inside the JavaScript Debug Terminal. Can be set to "off" to disable this behavior, or "always" to enable debugging in all terminals.

Name: debug.javascript.defaultRuntimeExecutable
Desc: The default `runtimeExecutable` used for launch configurations, if unspecified. This can be used to config custom paths to Node.js or browser installations.

Name: debug.javascript.enableNetworkView
Desc: Enables the experimental network view for targets that support it.

Name: debug.javascript.pickAndAttachOptions
Desc: Default options used when debugging a process through the `Debug: Attach to Node.js Process` command

Name: debug.javascript.resourceRequestOptions
Desc: Request options to use when loading resources, such as source maps, in the debugger. You may need to configure this if your sourcemaps require authentication or use a self-signed certificate, for instance. Options are used to create a request using the [`got`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/got) library. A common case to disable certificate verification can be done by passing `{ "https": { "rejectUnauthorized": false } }`.

Name: debug.javascript.terminalOptions
Desc: Default launch options for the JavaScript debug terminal and npm scripts.

Name: debug.javascript.unmapMissingSources
Desc: Configures whether sourcemapped file where the original file can't be read will automatically be unmapped. If this is false (default), a prompt is shown.

Name: dictation.enabled
Desc: Enables dictation across the product (chat input, editor, and terminal). When enabled on a supported platform, a microphone button appears in the chat input and the dictation shortcut becomes available; the on-device transcription model is downloaded on first use and runs locally.

Name: dictation.experimental.llmCleanup
Desc: Experimental: when dictation ends, the final transcript is passed through a small language model to restore punctuation, capitalization, paragraphs, and lists. Requires Copilot to be enabled; the transcript is sent to the language model for cleanup. Falls back to the raw transcript when no model is available. Use [dictation instructions](command:workbench.action.chat.configureDictationInstructions) to customize terminology and formatting.

Name: dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel
Desc: Controls the language model used for experimental dictation cleanup. `auto` follows the active experiment treatment.

Name: dictation.model
Desc: The model used for dictation. On-device models download on first use and run locally through Microsoft Foundry Local; the cloud option streams audio to the Microsoft AI voice service. - nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 multilingual streaming RNN-T, run on-device through Microsoft Foundry Local. Works offline; no audio leaves the device. Automatic language selection follows the Voice Mode language setting; when that setting is Automatic, dictation uses the configured display language when supported, then the system or browser locale, with model detection as a fallback. Downloaded on first use and cached on disk. - mai: Cloud transcription through the same Microsoft AI voice service used by Voice Mode. Requires a network connection and GitHub sign-in; audio is streamed to the service.

Name: dictation.showButton
Desc: Controls whether the dictation microphone button is shown in the chat input. When hidden, dictation can still be started with its keyboard shortcut.

Name: dictation.showTranscript
Desc: Controls whether the transcript is shown while dictating. The final transcript is inserted when dictation ends.

Name: diffEditor.codeLens
Desc: Controls whether the editor shows CodeLens.

Name: diffEditor.diffAlgorithm
Desc: - legacy: Uses the legacy diffing algorithm. - advanced: Uses the advanced diffing algorithm. - advanced-external: Uses the advanced diffing algorithm from the external `@vscode/diff` package (pure JavaScript). - advanced-wasm: Uses the advanced diffing algorithm from the external `@vscode/diff` package (WebAssembly).

Name: diffEditor.experimental.showEmptyDecorations
Desc: Controls whether the diff editor shows empty decorations to see where characters got inserted or deleted.

Name: diffEditor.experimental.showMoves
Desc: Controls whether the diff editor should show detected code moves.

Name: diffEditor.experimental.useTrueInlineView
Desc: If enabled and the editor uses the inline view, word changes are rendered inline.

Name: diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.contextLineCount
Desc: Controls how many lines are used as context when comparing unchanged regions.

Name: diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.enabled
Desc: Controls whether the diff editor shows unchanged regions.

Name: diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.minimumLineCount
Desc: Controls how many lines are used as a minimum for unchanged regions.

Name: diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.revealLineCount
Desc: Controls how many lines are used for unchanged regions.

Name: diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace
Desc: When enabled, the diff editor ignores changes in leading or trailing whitespace.

Name: diffEditor.maxComputationTime
Desc: Timeout in milliseconds after which diff computation is cancelled. Use 0 for no timeout.

Name: diffEditor.maxFileSize
Desc: Maximum file size in MB for which to compute diffs. Use 0 for no limit.

Name: diffEditor.renderGutterMenu
Desc: When enabled, the diff editor shows a special gutter for revert and stage actions.

Name: diffEditor.renderIndicators
Desc: Controls whether the diff editor shows +/- indicators for added/removed changes.

Name: diffEditor.renderMarginRevertIcon
